canada_place.subject: a long cruise-ship terminal pier building
canada_place.p8: Turn this into a crisp, sharp real aerial photograph at clear midday in Vancouver, British Columbia. The pale clay-grey 3D model is a long cruise-ship terminal pier building. Repaint it with real materials: white tensile-fabric sails with steel masts exist ONLY in the western (left) half, exactly where the model has sail shapes; the whole eastern (right) half is a plain flat white-grey roof deck with low railings and one flat pavilion roof, with no sails, no masts, no peaks and nothing standing on it; the pier walls are pale concrete with bands of dark glass, with the sea around. At the western end stands a tall hotel tower with white and dark glass horizontal bands. Strict edit: keep the exact outline, size, height and position of everything, keep every other building, street and the water exactly where they are, same framing and camera. Do not add any new building or object, and do not write any text or lettering.
canada_place.p9: Turn image 1, a soft aerial photograph, into a crisp, sharp, highly detailed real aerial photograph with exactly the geometry of image 2, a 3D render of the same place: every building stands exactly there. bc_place.subject: BC Place stadium in Vancouver: a round stadium with a white translucent fabric roof made of fine radial panels with a bright white central opening, a ring of tall white steel masts with thin steel cables, and pale grey concrete walls with a dark base band; one single round roof and one single central opening

rogers_arena.subject: Rogers Arena in Vancouver, an ice hockey arena: a large pale grey metal-clad flat roof with skylights and rooftop vents, curved dark glass and grey concrete concourse walls with green-grey cladding; real textured roofing, not a smooth white blob

harbour_centre.subject: Harbour Centre tower in Vancouver: a tall concrete and dark glass tower topped by a flying-saucer shaped revolving lookout disc with a ring of dark windows and a white and gold band, and a slim antenna above; exactly one disc, at the top of the shaft only

science_world.subject: Science World in Vancouver: a large geodesic sphere clad in silver-white triangular stainless-steel panels standing on a low cream-grey concrete building on the edge of False Creek, with a stone seawall below

marine_building.subject: the Marine Building in Vancouver: a 1930 art deco skyscraper clad in cream and pale green-grey terracotta with vertical piers and stepped setbacks, topped by the same low stepped crown as the model with a small low pale green copper roof, no taller than the model's crown

vancouver_house.subject: Vancouver House at the Granville Bridge: a slender twisted residential tower that is narrow at its base and widens upward, with white cantilevered balcony slabs and glass curtain walls

cp_skirt.subject: the pier base of a harbour pier
cp_skirt.p8: Turn this into a crisp, sharp real aerial photograph at clear midday in Vancouver. The grey-brown zone along the sea edge below the deck of this long pier is the pier's own base: a plain grey concrete wall with concrete piles and dark rock riprap reaching down into the sea, with no windows, no glass and no buildings. Strict edit: keep everything else exactly where it is, same framing and camera. Do not add any new building or object, and do not write any text or lettering.

ccw.subject: Vancouver Convention Centre West: a very large flat roof that is one continuous green living roof, a meadow of grasses and wildflowers in deep green with a few pale paths and skylights, on a waterfront building whose side walls are grey concrete and opaque dark glass, standing on a pier at the edge of the sea; solid and opaque, nothing seen through it
